prompts.title: Audit the current project and references
prompts.read: project.godot; scripts/core/game_services.gd; scripts/session/session_service.gd; scripts/world/colony_zones.gd; data/colony_manifest.json; all ten supplied screenshots.
prompts.goal: Create the implementation baseline for this pack. Inspect first; this prompt changes no gameplay.
build: Confirm the installed Godot version, executable paths, source-control state, main scene and current tests. Treat README machine paths as historical examples, not runnable local defaults.

Map the six requested rooms to actual zone IDs, station IDs and reachable interaction anchors. Capture the current HUD and each room. Verify Med Bay spawn, current crew-switch rules, survival timing and existing repair actions.
For R01-R10, record visible controls, feedback and what cannot be learned from a still image. Separate observations from inferred mechanics. Resolve the reference conflicts using page 5.
Write a concise baseline, risk list and changed-file ownership plan. Record which source .blend actually exists; only character .blend files were found in assets_src during this document audit.
checks: Provide exact paths and node IDs instead of invented anchors.
Run or explicitly mark unavailable the baseline compile/import and relevant existing suites; do not claim prior test results are current.
prompts.ask: Ask only if a room cannot be identified, supplied images cannot be read, or missing source assets prevent a required change. Continue unaffected audit work.

prompts.title: Define room, task and fault contracts
prompts.read: scripts/state/colony_state.gd; scripts/core/action_request.gd; action_result.gd; game_events.gd; scripts/session/action_service.gd; scripts/world/station_catalog.gd.
prompts.goal: Add the smallest shared data and action contract needed by the twelve repair tasks.
build: Define six stable room IDs and twelve stable task IDs from the room matrix. Each task has room_id, required specialty or general, interaction anchor, puzzle seed, fault generation, progress and current condition.

Keep first repair milestone, current operational condition and beauty-shot notification state separate. Two task milestones complete a room once; later wear can create maintenance work without erasing that achievement.

Use existing GameServices requests and host-side ActionService validation. Validate ownership, role, distance, room, fault generation and each accepted puzzle move. Do not trust a client completion boolean.
Define claim/release/timeout behavior for one active operator per puzzle; other players can run the other task in the room. Publish APIs and sample data; implement no room puzzle here.
checks: Duplicate completion requests apply their reward/repair once.
A stale move from an earlier fault generation is rejected; task and room IDs serialize predictably.
prompts.ask: Ask before replacing the existing action architecture or changing established mission progression. Choose additive contracts when possible.

prompts.title: Enforce specialist switching and co-op roles
prompts.read: scripts/state/character_state.gd; scripts/session/session_service.gd; existing claim_character validation; scripts/ui/crew_select_panel.gd.
prompts.goal: Require the correct specialist in both solo and multiplayer, following the user-confirmed solo rule.
build: Use electrical_comms, biology_food, medical_life_support and field_engineering_geology exactly as existing specialty IDs. General tasks accept any controlled character.

Solo players must switch to the required specialist; implement no solo role bypass. Keep all four specialists available through the existing safe crew-switch flow. Verify a reachable safe switching point from the Med Bay starting route.
In multiplayer, allow a differently specialized helper to complete a general task while the specialist works on the role task. Refuse the role task with a clear required-role message.

Revalidate on start, move, resume and completion. Release the puzzle on death, disconnect, character switch or loss of valid reach. Use existing crew ownership rules to prevent two peers claiming one character.
checks: For all twelve tasks, test correct role, wrong role and general access.
Complete a solo route using all four specialists; test two peers working on different tasks in one room.
Role switching while exposed cannot heal, refill equipment or clear exposure through an exploit.
prompts.ask: If existing safe switch rules make a required specialist inaccessible, present the specific conflict and a minimal safe-location change. Do not silently allow every role.

prompts.title: Persist and replicate new gameplay state
prompts.read: scripts/save/save_service.gd; save_migrations.gd; scripts/state/colony_state.gd; scripts/net/net_session.gd; tests/test_saves.gd; test_net_game.gd.
prompts.goal: Make task, cassette, wear and completion records survive saves and LAN synchronization.
build: Add versioned serialization and migration defaults for new room/task records, collected cassette IDs, puzzle seeds, fault generation, first-completion milestones and seen beauty-shot IDs.
Persist partial puzzle state only where its contract supports safe resume. Transient operator locks must not survive a restart; clear them on disconnect and allow a new eligible operator.

Replicate authoritative deltas or existing snapshots and events; late joiners reconstruct current world condition and task progress. Keep clients from writing host saves. Adjust protocol compatibility only if the actual wire schema requires it.
Specify exposure save behavior so reload cannot reset an ongoing lethal encounter; reuse existing recovery flow when necessary. Avoid offline deterioration unless separately authorized.
checks: Load an old save, save again and reopen without losing existing colony data.
Join late during a puzzle and after a room repair; reconnect with no stuck operator lock.
Replaying a request or reloading does not duplicate rewards or an already-seen completion shot.
prompts.ask: Ask if a migration would discard existing player progress. Do not overwrite test fixtures or real saves while diagnosing.

prompts.title: Build the shared task panel shell
prompts.read: scripts/ui/ui_panel.gd; ui_root.gd; ui_theme.gd; scripts/ui/hud/astra_style.gd; scripts/ui/ui_layout_check.gd.
prompts.goal: Provide a reusable native Godot panel frame that makes new puzzles belong to Mars Colony.
build: Reuse UiPanel/UiRoot and existing theme roles: navy/slate surfaces, orange primary actions, teal focus, off-white text and labeled status. Preserve current typography and text-size/high-contrast settings.
Support title, room, role, instructions, play area, progress, reset, cancel and success states. Free and restore the mouse correctly; prevent input leaking into movement or camera controls.
Provide keyboard equivalents for drag, rotate and timed activation. Add shapes/labels to color-coded objects. Show pending host validation and recover gracefully from a rejected or stale move.
Keep the world visible around in-game panels. Modal tasks and cassette reading never pause hazards. Critical alerts appear above the panel and can interrupt it safely. Build a dummy sample only.
checks: Check 1280x720 and 1920x1080, enlarged text and high contrast with no clipped controls.
Esc, cancel, death and disconnect restore focus and mouse capture correctly.
Opening the sample leaves authoritative simulation running.
prompts.ask: If theme conventions conflict, use the current station panel as the primary reference and document the decision. Ask before changing global HUD layout.

prompts.title: Place room anchors and Med Bay spawn
prompts.read: scenes/game.tscn; scripts/game/game_main.gd; scripts/core/game_services.gd; scripts/core/game_config.gd; scripts/world/station_catalog.gd; data/stations_*.json.
prompts.goal: Add reachable locations for the new interactions and establish Med Bay as the new-game spawn.
build: Map command_center to Command Room, power_supply to Power Room, greenhouse to the indoor Greenhouse, green_dome to Garden dome, med_bay to Med Bay, and hangar to Hangar bay with its linked Airlock task anchor.
Register two repair anchors and one cassette pickup per requested room. Add one cassette playback station only in Command Room. Use stable additive station data and measured Godot coordinates.

Set a collision-safe Med Bay spawn with a clear route to specialist switching and suits. Define recovery spawn consistently with the existing recovery system; do not move continuing players unexpectedly on normal load.
Keep cassette pickups, exits, suits and the playback station reachable in damaged rooms. Ensure the player can use the playback station before communications or wiring repairs.
checks: Walk to all nineteen new interactions: twelve tasks, six tapes and one player.
A new game spawns in Med Bay without floor penetration; continuing a save preserves its intended position.
Indoor Greenhouse and exterior Garden dome never share a task or cassette ID.
prompts.ask: Ask if the map lacks a safe Med Bay anchor or a requested room cannot be matched. Do not rebuild room geometry to guess a location.

prompts.title: Collect six room cassette tapes
prompts.read: Existing item/cargo interactions; scripts/player/carry_item.gd; scripts/session/action_service.gd; cassette state contract.
prompts.goal: Implement room cassette pickups and inventory metadata without remote playback.
build: Place one distinct labeled cassette in each of the six main rooms, including Command Room. A pickup reveals room title and collection status only; instructional pages are not readable there.

Use host validation for proximity and pickup. Proposed default: a colony-shared cassette library, with the physical pickup disappearing for everyone. Store stable cassette IDs independently of disposable cargo capacity.

Inventory shows collected/missing titles and the instruction "Play at Command Room cassette player." No hotkey, inventory action, alternate station or direct client request may display the instructional content.
Handle simultaneous pickup requests, save/load and late join. Make pickup objects clearly visible against existing room props and avoid collision traps.
checks: Six tapes can be collected exactly once and remain collected after load.
Two simultaneous pickups create one library entry.
Attempted playback away from the Command Room station fails on the host.
prompts.ask: Shared collection is a proposed default, not a user-confirmed ownership rule. Ask if personal inventories are required; otherwise implement the documented shared library.

prompts.title: Build the Command Room cassette player
prompts.read: UiPanel/UiRoot; station request validation; Command Room playback anchor from F06.
prompts.goal: Show a large two-column instructional overlay only while using the Command Room cassette player.
build: The station lists collected tapes and locked missing entries. Validate player ownership, interaction reach, station ID and Command Room zone before opening or changing a tape.

Use a centered rectangular frame around 82% viewport width and 76% height as an adjustable starting point. Leave visible world margins on every side and at the corners. Keep NASA image left and room instructions right; scale/scroll within the frame.

Provide room title, image caption, credit, source link, page navigation and close controls. Preserve image aspect ratio. This requirement is a visual/text briefing; do not invent required voice narration.
Close on loss of reach, death or station invalidation. Let hazards and other peers continue. Keep this station functional in the initial damaged command room to avoid a tutorial deadlock.
checks: Opening any of the six collected tapes works at the station and nowhere else.
Review both target resolutions and enlarged text; corners still reveal the world.
Critical warning and death interrupt playback without a stuck cursor.
prompts.ask: Ask only if physical audio or voiceover is additionally wanted; ship image/text playback under the current request.

prompts.title: Source and package real NASA imagery
prompts.read: scripts/ui/source_library.gd; source_register_panel.gd; data source/credit records; the NASA source appendix.
prompts.goal: Package at least one verified real NASA photograph for each cassette, with traceable source metadata.
build: Use the six official NASA candidates in the appendix as starting points. Choose the actual photograph in the page, not an author headshot, logo, render or unrelated inset. Confirm subject, image ID when available and credited creator.

Retrieve sufficient resolution for the left panel; package local optimized textures so gameplay requires no live internet. Record the official page, original asset URL, image ID, caption, credit, access date and any usage restrictions.

Preserve the photograph honestly; crop only for legibility and mark crops. A ground prototype must be labeled as a NASA ground project, and an ISS photograph must never be labeled as a real Mars colony.
Integrate credits with the existing source register and offline caption fallback. Review NASA media guidance and each image credit rather than assuming everything on nasa.gov has identical terms.
checks: All six tapes show actual photographs in an offline build.
Every bundled file has a matching source record and visible credit.
No placeholder, broken URL or unrelated portrait appears in the player.
prompts.ask: If a candidate is inaccessible or unsuitable, choose another official NASA asset and document why. Ask if no accurate photograph can support a required claim.

prompts.title: Write six room briefing scripts
prompts.read: Task pages in this pack; NASA captions and source records; existing in-game terminology.
prompts.goal: Create concise instructional text for every cassette using the actual implemented controls.
build: Write one briefing per room, about 120-180 words each, split into readable pages if needed. Cover the room purpose, both tasks, required specialist, general helper role, controls, success cues and relevant hazards.

Use the six draft briefing seeds in the appendix, then align them with final puzzle behavior. Mention solo players must switch specialists. Explain the suit and pressure warning in the Hangar briefing.
Describe NASA photographs accurately in a separate caption. Separate documented NASA hardware from fictional game repair procedures, invented nutrient tokens and gameplay death timing.
Use plain language and match current action labels exactly. Briefings may help players but are not required to unlock the repair tasks; include local task instructions too.
checks: A new player can describe the first input and success condition for all twelve tasks after reading.
No briefing advertises a control or mechanic absent from its puzzle.
All six display correctly with their matching left-side photo and source.
prompts.ask: Ask about audience age or narration only if it materially changes required content; otherwise use accessible general-audience text and no new voice service.

prompts.title: Make unprotected exposure lethal in four seconds
prompts.read: scripts/session/session_service.gd::advance; scripts/sim/colony_sim.gd; life_support_model.gd; scripts/core/game_balance.gd; recovery flow.
prompts.goal: Replace the very slow unprotected exterior survival with immediate danger and about four real seconds to death/recovery.
build: Add a host-authoritative exposure timer using elapsed unpaused real seconds, independent of sol length and game-hours resource consumption. Start on entry into an unbreathable zone without a functional sealed suit and breathable reserve.

Default lethal deadline: 4.0 seconds, with simulation-step tolerance. Apply immediate danger state and invoke the existing character recovery/death pathway exactly once at the deadline; prevent double health damage or duplicate recoveries.

Safe breathable shelter or a valid protective suit ends the lethal condition. Prevent repeated boundary crossings, reload, equipment toggles or character switches from giving a free full timer; use an explicit safe-recovery interval.

Recompute from authoritative position and pressure/protection state, including a failed airlock. Keep existing non-exposure health needs and suited resource accounting intact. Use a configurable gameplay rule, not a claim about human physiology.
checks: From healthy start, unprotected exposure resolves at 4.0 seconds +/- one hazard step across low/high frame rates and sol lengths.
A valid suit protects until its reserve fails; safe zones do not kill.
Task UI, cassette UI, client menus and cinematics cannot freeze the timer.
prompts.ask: Retain the existing recovery semantics unless the owner requests permanent death. Ask if recovery is incompatible with Med Bay spawn design.

prompts.title: Add unmistakable fatal-exposure warnings
prompts.read: scripts/game/game_hud.gd; scripts/ui/hud/vitals_bar.gd; toast_stack.gd; UiTheme urgent styles; existing audio/subtitle settings.
prompts.goal: Warn immediately and visibly when a player enters a lethal atmosphere.
build: Show a bright urgent banner, danger border and labeled countdown: "NO BREATHABLE AIR - SUIT REQUIRED" or an accurate pressure/suit-reserve cause. Use a warning symbol and text, not color alone.
Add a brief alarm using existing audio preferences. Keep a reduced-flash option and readable static urgent mode. Never obscure the escape route or the puzzle cancel control.
Display above task and cassette panels; update from authoritative remaining exposure time with smooth local presentation. Remove it only after validated safety or recovery.

For airlock failure, identify the affected area and useful action: reach safe pressure, equip a suit, or seal the leak with the field engineer. Do not make specialist repair the only escape within four seconds.
checks: The warning appears within one host update on entry and is visible over every modal panel.
Silent audio, high contrast and reduced flash still communicate imminent death.
Two peers see their own hazard correctly; no stale countdown remains after recovery.
prompts.ask: If a global overlay layer blocks existing menus or alerts, fix its stacking and input behavior within this prompt rather than replacing the HUD.

prompts.title: Run faster equipment degradation continuously
prompts.read: Existing equipment condition and repair actions; GameBalance; PowerModel; LifeSupportModel; SessionService simulation timing.
prompts.goal: Make maintainable equipment visibly deteriorate throughout active play without relying on room entry or open panels.
build: Inventory existing condition-bearing equipment first. Add configurable wear rates and thresholds for the six repair systems while preserving resource ledgers and real-vs-game-time units. Do not add a second ticker for existing equipment.

Proposed playtest defaults: a measurable condition change within 30 seconds, warning near 2 minutes and a maintenance fault near 4 minutes on neglected newly repaired equipment. Treat these as tuning targets, not settled owner requirements.

Run from the authoritative session throughout active gameplay, including tasks, cassette playback and beauty shots. Respect an actual global pause; a local menu is not a global pause. Unloaded presentation nodes must not stop wear.

Repairs restore only their mapped system and clear the current fault. Use hysteresis/cooldowns to prevent immediate re-faulting. Preserve first-repair achievements and one-time beauty-shot records during recurring maintenance.
checks: Timed idle play with panels open and closed produces equivalent wear.
Save/load, late join and two clients agree on condition; no doubled degradation.
Repairs improve the correct system and recurring faults remain possible without replaying mission rewards.
prompts.ask: Ask for a desired difficulty target if the proposed cadence makes the twelve-task route infeasible; expose rates in balance data instead of hard-coding them.

prompts.title: Connect pressure faults to safe playable hazards
prompts.read: GameServices outside_test; ColonyZones; LifeSupportModel cabin pressure; door_controller.gd; Garden dome doors; airlock diagnostic tools.
prompts.goal: Make hangar/airlock failure dangerous while preserving a solvable, protected route to repair.
build: Add a small explicit pressure/protection query covering the affected airlock volume. Lighting-zone membership alone must not imply breathable air. Keep the enclosed Garden dome safe unless an explicit fault is meant to depressurize it.

Link the airlock seal condition to pressure loss, doors/interlocks, warning state and the exposure model. Avoid instant whole-colony decompression from one local fault unless existing simulation topology actually supports it.
Provide an accessible working suit or safe-side repair interaction before the fatal volume. A 20-45 second repair must not force an unprotected player to survive a four-second hazard.

Use a localized pressure model or existing cabin model consistently; document mass/pressure coupling and prevent duplicate air loss. Add a controlled debug fault trigger for verification, not a player-facing cheat.
checks: Trigger a leak: unsuited entry warns and kills on schedule, while a properly suited engineer can repair it.
Sealing stops the leak and restores safe pressure through a readable recovery state.
Door thresholds do not create flickering safe/danger states or bypass the suit check.
prompts.ask: Ask before introducing a full fluid simulation or colony-wide pressure rewrite. Implement the smallest correct local hazard integration.

prompts.title: Command: tune the communications link
prompts.read: R02 communications image; shared panel and task contracts; existing communications/data systems.
prompts.goal: Implement only the general Command Room communications task, inspired by waveform tuning.
build: Show target and received waveforms and one tuning dial/keyboard slider. Adjust frequency; propose a second amplitude adjustment only if a single dial is too trivial. Label both traces in game style.

Use a seeded target and a tolerant match window. Holding a valid match for an adjustable short interval locks the link, then a visible data-transfer bar reaches a validated completion. A static screenshot does not specify the exact original thresholds.

Accept any specialty. Keep playback station functionality separate so a failed comms task never disables cassette education. Cancelling leaves a safely resumable task or restarts its small puzzle under the shared contract.
On completion, restore the mapped communications condition and emit the shared repair event; do not repair wiring or complete the entire room.
checks: The target is reachable with mouse and keyboard, and false matches cannot complete transfer.
A wrong specialist is still allowed because this is general.
Success changes only comms, and a helper can do it while an electrical specialist works on wires.
prompts.ask: R02 shows tuning, not a complete data protocol. Ask if a specific data-transfer interaction is required; otherwise use the labeled tuning-plus-transfer design.

prompts.title: Command: reconnect the wiring panel
prompts.read: R03 wires image; shared task shell; electrical_comms role validation.
prompts.goal: Implement only the Command Room specialist wiring puzzle.
build: Present four left terminals and four shuffled right terminals. Drag or select a left terminal, then connect its matching right terminal. Give every pair a unique label/symbol as well as a theme-compatible cable color.

Draw flexible cables with readable crossing and endpoint feedback. A wrong connection explains the mismatch and releases; correct connections lock or can be deliberately disconnected before final verification.
The host validates terminal IDs, uniqueness, the current seeded mapping and actor specialty. Complete only when all four pairs are correctly connected.
Restore the wiring condition and trigger the shared partial-room improvement. Use original in-game assets and console framing; do not import the reference screenshot as the task UI.
checks: All four pairs must match; repeated or forged endpoint IDs fail.
Medical, biology and field engineering characters are blocked in solo and co-op.
Keyboard-only play, cable crossing and color-blind identification remain clear.
prompts.ask: Use one four-pair board initially. Ask before adding multiple panels or a long multi-stage sequence beyond the current room scope.

prompts.title: Power: calibrate the three distributor rings
prompts.read: R09 numbered circles and timing bars; task shell; PowerModel equipment mapping.
prompts.goal: Implement only the general Power Room circle timing game.
build: Use three numbered rotating rings, each with a pointer and a marked alignment sector, paired with a charge/progress indicator. Players activate the current ring while the pointer is inside the sector.

A successful timing hit locks that channel and advances to the next. Proposed miss behavior: reset only the active ring, with a clear cue; keep speed, sector width and accessibility assistance configurable.
Calculate success on the host timeline, accounting for the existing request path. Do not accept a client "hit=true" flag. Provide an explicit accessibility setting for a wider timing window.
Any role may calibrate. Restoring the distributor condition affects its mapped power function only; the specialist circuit task remains independent.
checks: All three channels are required; misses do not falsely lock a channel.
The game is playable at low frame rate and representative LAN latency.
A biologist can finish this general task while an electrical specialist works on circuits.
prompts.ask: R09 is a still image; the timing sequence is an inferred design. Ask if a different circle-game variant was intended before replacing it with another mechanic.

prompts.title: Power: route and balance an electrical circuit
prompts.read: R10 circuit screenshot: inventory, rotation, fixed cells, current path, actual and target voltage.
prompts.goal: Implement only the electrical/comms specialist circuit puzzle in Power Room.
build: Create one small grid with source, destination, fixed/blocked cells and limited straight/elbow conductor pieces. Support select, place, quarter-turn, remove and reset with keyboard equivalents.

Add a small number of labeled positive/negative voltage components. Require both a continuous correctly oriented route and the displayed target net voltage. Show actual versus target and animate current only along a valid connected path.

Use an authored known-solvable board first; validate solvability and inventory counts. Host verification checks adjacency ports, source-to-goal connectivity, piece limits, fixed cells and voltage arithmetic.
Restrict to electrical_comms. Success restores the mapped circuit system only and feeds shared room progression. Keep this distinct from the general timing rings.
checks: A connected route with the wrong voltage fails, and correct voltage without a connected route also fails.
Reset restores the initial inventory; removal cannot duplicate pieces.
Correct role can solve with no drag input; forged completion is rejected.
prompts.ask: Ask before adding random circuit generation, complex branching electrical simulation or multiple difficulty boards. One polished solvable board satisfies this prompt.

prompts.title: Greenhouse: balance the plant element network
prompts.read: R05 plant-attribute hex network; indoor Greenhouse anchors; CropSystem and biology_food role.
prompts.goal: Implement only the indoor Greenhouse biologist element puzzle.
build: Preserve the reference skeleton: connected hex tokens, attribute icons/counters, a target profile and a plant preview. Use game-native plant, moisture, light and nutrient symbols rather than the source game artwork.

Proposed mechanic: place a limited set of nutrient/light/water attribute tokens into a small connected hex network, rotating connector edges where needed. Meet the displayed target counts and connectivity constraints; preview the plant response.

Use explicit token contributions and a known solution. Do not describe invented combinations as real chemical practice. Show why a count or connection is invalid and offer reset without consuming colony resources during experimentation.
Only biology_food can operate. Validate counts, inventory and connectivity on the host; completion restores the nutrient/growth-control fault, leaving watering as a separate general task.
checks: Correct counts with broken connectivity fail; a connected wrong profile also fails.
The authored board has a verified solution and no duplicate-token exploit.
Only the biologist succeeds, including after solo character switching.
prompts.ask: R05 cannot prove exact Spider-Man 2 rules. Ask if exact adjacency/attribute rules are essential; otherwise use this labeled, reference-inspired design.

prompts.title: Greenhouse: redirect water into the plant bed
prompts.read: R01 falling droplets and movable angled guides; indoor Greenhouse; existing water/crop ledgers.
prompts.goal: Implement only the general indoor plant-watering task, retaining the reference stream-guidance play.
build: Show a nozzle, plant bed and two adjustable guide plates. Players reposition/rotate the plates to redirect a visible water stream into the target instead of clicking a generic "water" button.

Prefer a deterministic lightweight stream/path model with droplets as presentation, so the puzzle is stable across frame rates and peers. Fill the moisture gauge only when the validated path reaches the bed.

Use a configurable target fill and cap. Apply the real colony water cost through existing ledger APIs once accepted, without charging again on retries or allowing visual particles to create resources.
Any character can operate. Clear moisture and plant response cues signal success; restore only irrigation/watering condition and emit shared task completion.
checks: A stream that misses the bed earns no progress.
Both guides can be controlled without a mouse; reset always gives a solvable state.
Success consumes the intended finite water once and leaves the element task incomplete.
prompts.ask: R01 supports stream routing but not exact physics. Use the simple stable model; ask before introducing a separate fluid engine or requiring realistic microgravity behavior.

prompts.title: Garden dome: connect the irrigation pipes
prompts.read: R04 pipes, water and pump imagery; Garden dome anchors, not indoor Greenhouse.
prompts.goal: Implement only the field engineer pipe-connection puzzle in the exterior garden dome.
build: Show a compact scrambled board with source pump, destination planter and a few straight/elbow pipe sections. Rotate or place sections to connect their matching ports, with a small number of harmless dead ends.
Keep the solution simple and authored. Host validation checks port adjacency, source-to-destination connectivity and any required end cap; matching appearance alone is insufficient.

After validation, animate water filling connected segments in order, then update the corresponding world pipe flow. Use a shader or lightweight particles, with a static flow indicator for reduced motion.
Only field_engineering_geology may complete. Restore irrigation condition only; leave glass repair independent. The enclosed dome stays breathable unless its explicit pressure fault says otherwise.
checks: A gap, misrotated elbow or disconnected destination fails.
Water visibly traverses the solved route and the matching world pipes.
The field engineer can solve in solo and co-op; other roles receive a clear restriction.
prompts.ask: The image does not specify a grid size. Use a small solvable board and ask only if the owner needs a specific layout or exact reference-game rules.

prompts.title: Garden dome: assemble the replacement glass pane
prompts.read: R06 irregular grid/shape puzzle; user request for about five loose pieces forming a square.
prompts.goal: Implement only the general glass repair task, following the spoken square-pane requirement.
build: Give the player approximately five disorganized polygon pieces and a square target frame. Drag/select, move and rotate pieces into a complete square; use a snap tolerance and clear legal-placement preview.

Borrow the reference shape-fitting logic and tiled visual organization. R06 shows region partitioning, not proof of a five-piece square assembly; prioritize the requested assembly rather than reproducing that different puzzle.
Author a guaranteed tiling. The host checks piece identity, allowed transforms, bounds, no overlap and complete target coverage. Invalid placements do not lose a piece.
Any role may repair. Success fuses the visual pane, replaces only the mapped broken glazing and clears its repair fault. Do not also fix irrigation or complete the room early.
checks: All pieces are required; overlap, holes and off-frame placement fail.
Mouse and keyboard play can complete the square with generous snapping.
The restored world pane appears for both peers and after load.
prompts.ask: Ask only if exact grid-region partitioning is desired instead of the spoken square assembly. Default to the five-piece square pane stated by the user.

prompts.title: Med Bay: prepare the guided test-tube mixture
prompts.read: R08 layered liquid tubes; medical_life_support role; Med Bay station anchor.
prompts.goal: Implement only the medical specialist chemical-preparation task with clear visual guidance.
build: Show labeled reagent tubes, a highlighted destination and an illustrated target recipe with quantities/order. Select a source and destination to pour a controlled unit, with visible fill levels and capacity checks.

Use the reference pouring animation and layered liquid readability. The screenshot resembles liquid sorting, but the user requested guided mixing; use a fictional diagnostic reagent recipe rather than silently changing the goal to color sorting.
Show a safe error explanation for wrong order, quantity or destination and allow reset. Use invented reagent codes; include no real medical treatment or hazardous chemical recipe.
Restrict to medical_life_support. The host validates pour sequence, remaining quantities, destination and final recipe. Success restores the reagent/diagnostic preparation system only.
checks: An incorrect destination, overflow or wrong recipe cannot complete.
Correct labeled amounts and sequence produce a clear success cue independent of color.
Only the medical specialist operates; the general equipment task remains available to others.
prompts.ask: Ask if the owner intended exact liquid sorting instead of guided mixing. The documented default follows the spoken mixing instructions.

prompts.title: Med Bay: plug in and verify the equipment
prompts.read: R07 wall socket, plug and tether; Med Bay equipment; existing station power model.
prompts.goal: Implement only the general Med Bay connection and equipment-check task.
build: Show an unplugged device and clearly labeled compatible socket. Let the player drag or select the plug and socket, seat the connection, then run a short self-test.
Use orientation/keying or matching labels for a small interaction challenge; never require color alone. Animate cable and device indicators using game-native assets.

The host validates connector/socket IDs and the subsequent self-test. Display distinct connected, powered and verified states, with a readable reason for a failed test. Map failure to repairable local task state without forcing a dependency on another room.
Any role can complete. Restore only the mapped medical device condition; the specialist reagent task still needs its own completion.
checks: Wrong socket and incomplete insertion fail; inserting alone does not skip the self-test.
Any of the four specialties can complete the full flow.
Reload or peer disconnect during the test does not mark success without host validation.
prompts.ask: R07 is only a connection cue. Keep this small and approachable; ask before adding a large troubleshooting tree or new multi-room power dependency.

prompts.title: Hangar: remove the tracked-in Mars dust
prompts.read: Hangar bay geometry, suit racks and airlock entry route; theme and shared task APIs.
prompts.goal: Design and implement only the general hangar-dusting task using the project aesthetic.
build: Create a close-up work panel for one reachable hangar cleaning station. Show a small surface map with several dusty patches representing entry mats, equipment and suit staging surfaces.
Move a brush/vacuum tool across patches while holding an action; keyboard navigation selects a patch and holds the same cleaning action. Reveal clean material and a labeled cleanliness gauge.

Validate tool coverage or bounded cleaning increments on the host, with a reasonable operation rate. Stop progress on cancel or loss of reach. Keep visual dust particles cheap and provide reduced-motion feedback.
Any role may clean. Success reduces the mapped hangar dust burden, removes the corresponding visible patches and restores only cleanliness condition. Use no external game branding.
checks: Untouched patches cannot be marked clean by a forged completion flag.
Both control methods can finish; cancel/resume remains consistent.
General dusting can run while a field engineer repairs the airlock.
prompts.ask: No reference image was supplied and the user authorized invention. Make routine art/mechanic choices autonomously; ask only about conflicts with existing hangar interactions.

prompts.title: Hangar: locate and seal the airlock leak
prompts.read: Airlock doors/interlocks; pressure fault contract; field_engineering_geology role; shared puzzle shell.
prompts.goal: Design and implement only the specialist airlock-sealing task linked to the hangar.
build: Provide a safe-side or suited repair interaction showing an airlock cross-section, pressure gauge and visible airflow at a damaged seal. First identify the leaking segment using a simple diagnostic indicator.
Seat the correct gasket/patch, then tighten a small set of numbered fasteners in a displayed order. Finish with an explicit pressure-hold test. Use clear progress and recoverable mistakes.

Only field_engineering_geology can operate. Host validation checks leak ID, patch placement, fastener sequence and final seal test before clearing the pressure fault; clicking the diagram is not sufficient.

Stop the leak and show pressure recovering, then restore safe door state according to the interlock. Keep the four-second hazard active for unprotected players; do not pause or grant hidden immunity during the puzzle.
checks: An unsealed fault causes pressure danger and scheduled unsuited death.
A correctly suited engineer can complete all steps and observe stable safe pressure.
Others can dust concurrently, and no door cycle reopens a completed seal unintentionally.
prompts.ask: No reference was supplied. Use this small original design; ask before adding suit failure, whole-colony evacuation or a much longer emergency sequence.

prompts.title: Establish additive Blender and Godot repair assets
prompts.read: data/palette.json; materials/colony_surface.gdshader; tools/export_from_blender.ps1; tools/blender/export_colony_glb.py; current world nodes.
prompts.goal: Create a safe repeatable asset path for damaged, partial and repaired room presentations.
build: Confirm the actual colony source .blend. The export script contains a historical G: path; do not assume it exists. If unavailable, use additive Godot scenes and matching materials rather than overwriting the imported colony.

Keep new Blender work in a dedicated derivative file under assets_src. Use named collections, consistent scale/origins, applied transforms and stable export names; preserve existing source files and object IDs.

Define a common visual binding manifest from task IDs to damaged/repaired props, material parameters, lights and lightweight effects. Presentation reads authoritative state; it never decides completion.

Create reusable debris, cracked-pane overlay, disconnected cable and dust assets matching the flat-shaded colony palette. Keep routes, spawn, suits and interaction anchors usable. Verify GLB normals/materials and collision after import.
checks: A test prop looks consistent in Blender export and Godot lighting.
Regenerating the world does not delete additive repairs or change existing stable station IDs.
Document asset counts/performance against the measured baseline; avoid unique heavy geometry per room.
prompts.ask: Ask for a missing source .blend only when required for geometry that cannot be handled additively. Never save over a user original to make a derivative.

prompts.title: Stage Command Room damage and restoration
prompts.read: Command Room scene/anchors; communication and wiring task state.
prompts.goal: Give Command Room visible initial damage and distinct improvements from each of its two tasks.
build: Initial state: dim or unstable console indicators, open cable access and a visibly disconnected communications display. Add small safe debris; keep the cassette player illuminated and usable.

Communications repair stabilizes the link display and its labeled status; wiring repair seats cable covers and restores its associated light group. Both task orders must produce correct partial states.
When both systems are currently repaired, show a clean, functional console room with coherent lighting and active non-branded telemetry. Bind each effect through the shared visual manifest.
Apply condition thresholds to later wear without erasing the first-repair milestone. Use deterministic props/materials rather than random geometry on every load.
checks: Capture damaged, comms-only, wires-only and fully restored states from identical angles.
Both peers and a loaded save display the same task-to-visual state.
Cassette player and exits remain reachable in every state.
prompts.ask: Ask if a required fixture cannot be identified. Do not replace the entire room or change the established console color language.

prompts.title: Stage Power Room damage and restoration
prompts.read: Power Room geometry; PowerModel; ring and circuit task mappings.
prompts.goal: Show separate distributor and circuit repairs transforming the Power Room.
build: Initial state: unstable distributor rings, disconnected local circuit indicators, safe sparks behind shielding and modest cable clutter. Avoid disabling the whole colony as an incidental art effect.
Circle calibration stabilizes the three numbered channel indicators. Circuit completion restores its local bus trace and secured panel cover. Keep electrical effects tied to actual state.
Fully restored presentation shows steady indicators, secured wiring and clean equipment surfaces. Use controlled emissive materials; prevent light spill into adjacent zones.
Provide deterministic transitions for both task orders and future worn-condition thresholds through the shared manifest. No art script grants electrical output or mission completion.
checks: Compare damaged, each partial state and restored screenshots.
Visual indicators agree with host power state and remain readable at current exposure settings.
Added effects do not obstruct the operator or cause a significant frame-time regression.
prompts.ask: Ask before coupling a local art repair to colony-wide power shedding. Keep any real power changes in the validated gameplay layer.

prompts.title: Stage indoor Greenhouse restoration
prompts.read: Indoor Greenhouse fixtures, CropSystem and both greenhouse task states.
prompts.goal: Transform the indoor Greenhouse progressively through plant-profile and watering repairs.
build: Show wilted but recoverable crops, dry bed indicators and unstable local grow-control displays at entry. Keep indoor identity distinct from the outside Garden dome.

Element-network repair stabilizes nutrient/grow-light control visuals. Watering repair adds appropriate moisture and local irrigation activity. Neither action alone instantly completes both task effects.
Fully restored state shows healthier plant posture/color, steady grow lights and readable moisture feedback. Use an attractive transition without pretending mature crops physically grow in seconds.
Use material/mesh variants or lightweight animation, not expensive real-time plant simulation. Bind visual decline to current equipment/crop condition while preserving narrative repair milestones.
checks: Both partial repair orders read clearly and persist through reload.
Plants and water effects match accepted task state rather than local UI animation.
The Garden dome task state does not affect these indoor props.
prompts.ask: Ask if existing crop growth already drives the same meshes; merge the visual drivers so neither system overwrites the other.

prompts.title: Stage Garden dome glass and flowing water
prompts.read: Garden dome glazing and pipe meshes; shared visual bindings; garden_dome_doors.gd.
prompts.goal: Make glass assembly and irrigation repair visibly restore the outside plant dome.
build: Initial state: clearly cracked or missing replacement pane overlays and interrupted irrigation with stressed plants. Preserve traversal collision and safe doors; do not create an unmodeled pressure leak through an art-only crack.
Pipe repair animates water through the mapped world segments in source-to-bed order. Glass repair replaces the mapped broken pane with a continuous intact surface; each can happen first.
Fully repaired state must visibly show both continuous glazing and flowing water. Adjust transparency and camera sightlines so the result can be seen under existing dome lighting.
Use efficient flow UVs/shaders and a reduced-motion state. Bind later maintenance visuals to actual conditions while maintaining the one-time room achievement.
checks: Record damaged, pipes-only, glass-only and restored views.
The completed view clearly exposes water flow and an intact pane in-game.
No transparency sorting or collider change blocks movement or makes the dome disappear.
prompts.ask: Ask before removing original glazing geometry if that risks imported hierarchy or collision. Prefer named additive replacements and reversible visibility changes.

prompts.title: Stage Med Bay damage and restoration
prompts.read: Med Bay spawn, medical device props and chemical-preparation station.
prompts.goal: Restore Med Bay visually while keeping it a safe understandable starting room.
build: Start with disorganized reagent trays, disconnected equipment, dim status displays and minor contained damage. Protect the spawn capsule/arrival area and a clear exit route.
Medical preparation success organizes the reagent station and marks its diagnostic supply ready. General equipment success seats cables and starts the corresponding monitor/self-test indicator.
Fully restored state shows clean work surfaces, functioning medical monitors and labeled ready supplies, with the same colony palette. Avoid invented real treatment instructions on screens.
Bind each partial state through stable nodes; reconnect after load or scene rebuild. New-game damage initialization must not reset completed saves.
checks: A player spawns, looks around and reaches both stations without collision or visual obstruction.
Each task independently changes its correct prop group.
A fully repaired saved room loads restored without replaying its initial damage animation.
prompts.ask: Ask before moving the established Med Bay spawn or recovery anchor to improve a camera angle. Adjust props/camera instead when possible.

prompts.title: Stage Hangar dust and airlock restoration
prompts.read: Hangar bay, suit racks, airlock geometry and pressure/cleanliness state.
prompts.goal: Make cleaning and seal repair produce separate visible hangar improvements.
build: Initial state: tracked dust at entry and equipment staging, plus a readable localized seal leak with airflow trails and urgent airlock indicators. Keep usable suits and the safe-side console accessible.
Dusting removes the mapped dust overlays and debris without stopping the leak. Sealing suppresses leak effects and shows pressure recovering without automatically cleaning the floor.

Fully restored state has clean staging surfaces, organized suit area and an airlock indicator that reports the actual verified pressure/seal state. Keep door behavior tied to interlocks, not animation timing.
Use modest particles and material overlays; preserve transparency, collision and performance. Future faults restore only the affected visual damage.
checks: Dust-only and seal-only states are clearly distinguishable.
The fully restored airlock has no leak particles while pressure is safe.
Suits, doors and repair interaction remain usable throughout every transition.
prompts.ask: Ask if the suit rack area overlaps the requested hangar anchor; resolve the mapping explicitly instead of relocating suit functionality silently.

prompts.title: Build the safe room-completion camera controller
prompts.deps: F04, F05, S01-S04; shared room events
prompts.read: scripts/player/player_camera_rig.gd; GameEvents; UiRoot; camera ownership and motion settings.
prompts.goal: Create a reusable short beauty-shot controller triggered after a room first completes both repairs.
build: Subscribe to host-validated first-completion events carrying a unique room/milestone ID. Keep six data-driven camera paths separate from task logic. Proposed duration: 5-7 seconds, skippable, with reduced-motion alternative.

Playback is local presentation; do not force other peers away from their own tasks. Proposed default: notify all peers, play for the completing player when safe, offer others a safe replay option. Record seen state appropriately.

Continue simulation and degradation. Defer shots if the local player is exposed, performing a task or otherwise unsafe; immediately abort on danger, death, disconnect or a critical panel. Do not grant hidden invulnerability.
On every exit restore the previous camera, mouse mode, input, HUD and audio. Queue simultaneous room events without losing them or replaying duplicates.
checks: Both tasks are required, in either order; a room shot is offered once for its first milestone.
Skip, death, alarm, save/load and disconnect leave the player controllable.
Another peer continues play and hazards keep ticking during the shot.
prompts.ask: Ask if all players must watch simultaneously; do not implement a forced global cutscene under the proposed local-playback default.

prompts.title: Author the Command Room beauty shot
prompts.read: Command Room measured camera clearance and restored prop groups.
prompts.goal: Author only the Command Room camera path and shot binding.
build: Plan a 5-7 second gentle pan from the secured wiring panel across the stable comms displays to the cassette player. End on a clear wide view of the repaired room.
Use existing camera conventions and lighting. Keep the camera inside walls, outside prop collision and away from ceilings or clipped cable geometry. No full orbit is required if the room is narrow.
Trigger only after both command task milestones. Show live restored state; if a fresh hazard invalidates the view, defer or abort through V01 rather than faking a completed system.
Provide a static composed view for reduced motion and a usable skip hint. Save only shot metadata, not temporary camera ownership.
checks: Verify the entire path at actual aspect ratios with no wall clipping or hidden focal props.
The frame shows stable comms and repaired wiring together.
Skip and normal completion both restore the player camera and controls.
prompts.ask: If a pan cannot fit the room, use a shorter dolly or static-to-static transition and document the spatial constraint.

prompts.title: Author the Power Room beauty shot
prompts.read: Power Room camera clearance; restored rings, circuit bus and lighting.
prompts.goal: Author only the Power Room repair-completion shot.
build: Start on the now-stable distributor channels, pan to the restored circuit panel and finish on the functional local power equipment.
Compose emissive displays so they retain readable detail instead of blooming to white. Preserve existing room exposure and light-layer boundaries.
Bind the shot to first completion of both Power Room tasks; reuse V01 safety, skip and restoration handling. Do not add a second task-completion listener with independent rewards.
Include reduced-motion composition and record a representative screenshot for each endpoint.
checks: Both task results are recognizable in the shot and the camera stays inside the room.
No unsafe state forces playback or freezes power degradation.
Camera/FOV/input restore on skip and completion.
prompts.ask: If existing props hide the electrical route, adjust the shot or add a small matching status indicator; ask before remodeling the room.

prompts.title: Author the indoor Greenhouse beauty shot
prompts.read: Indoor Greenhouse plants, grow-control fixtures and irrigation visuals.
prompts.goal: Author only the indoor Greenhouse repair-completion shot.
build: Use a gentle lateral pan along the restored plant beds, showing healthy plant presentation, stable grow-control lights and moisture/irrigation cues.
Finish with a wide indoor composition that cannot be mistaken for the exterior Garden dome. Keep plants from occluding the entire frame and avoid passing through foliage meshes.
Bind to the two indoor greenhouse milestones through V01. Keep the growth/condition presentation live and do not force instantaneous crop harvest or a resource reward from the camera script.
Supply a reduced-motion static frame, skip hint and evidence of the full path in the current renderer.
checks: The camera shows the effects of both element and watering tasks.
No dome-state event triggers this shot; no walls or plant meshes clip the camera.
Interruptions return control without changing crop state.
prompts.ask: Ask if the present crop presentation cannot communicate repair clearly; propose a modest prop/material change rather than adding another task.

prompts.title: Author the Garden dome water-and-glass beauty shot
prompts.read: Exterior Garden dome camera clearance, repaired glazing and world pipe-flow effect.
prompts.goal: Author only the Garden dome completion shot, emphasizing the two outcomes the user specified.
build: Begin close enough to see water moving through repaired pipes, follow the flow toward the plant beds, then pan upward or outward to reveal a continuous intact glass pane.
Choose the path against real transparency and lighting, not an editor-only view. Keep repaired glazing legible and ensure water motion remains visible at normal game resolution.
Use the first completion of both dome tasks to request V01 playback. If current irrigation/pressure is unsafe or newly failed, defer rather than displaying an inaccurate pre-rendered success movie.
Provide a static view that contains both pipe and glass results for reduced motion; include named camera anchors and framing evidence.
checks: An observer can identify visible flowing water and connected unbroken glazing.
No dome shell clipping or transparency disappearance occurs along the path.
Skip, interruption and late join behave according to V01.
prompts.ask: Ask only if existing pipe placement makes both effects impossible to show; propose a short two-part camera move before changing world geometry.

prompts.title: Author the Med Bay beauty shot
prompts.read: Med Bay restored stations and safe spawn/recovery area.
prompts.goal: Author only the Med Bay repair-completion shot.
build: Pan from the organized reagent station to the now-powered medical monitor and finish on a readable clean Med Bay wide shot.
Keep the spawn/recovery area visible enough to orient the player without passing through a bed or medical device. Screens should show fictional ready/self-test information, not clinical instructions.
Bind to both Med Bay task milestones through V01. A recovering player must receive control and warnings promptly; defer this shot while recovery or another critical flow is active.
Include reduced-motion frame, skip support and clear return to the original camera mode.
checks: Both task improvements appear clearly and the player can orient after the shot.
No spawn or recovery position is moved by camera playback.
Death/recovery, skip and normal completion restore input reliably.
prompts.ask: If room size limits movement, use a short gentle pan from a safe corner rather than clipping through the medical fixtures.

prompts.title: Author the Hangar and sealed-airlock beauty shot
prompts.read: Hangar clean surfaces, suit racks and sealed airlock pressure indicators.
prompts.goal: Author only the Hangar completion shot.
build: Pan across the cleaned entry/staging area toward organized suits and finish on the sealed airlock with a legible safe-pressure indicator.
Frame the absence of leak airflow with the positive seal-test result so success reads as more than a particle effect disappearing. Keep door safety/interlock logic live.
Use V01 only after dust and airlock repair milestones, and only when the local player is safe. If pressure falls again mid-shot, interrupt immediately and show the hazard warning.
Provide a composed reduced-motion frame, skippable playback and smooth return to the player camera.
checks: Clean floor and a verified sealed airlock are both recognizable.
A debug pressure failure interrupts the shot and never grants survival immunity.
No camera path crosses the airlock door or blocks a suit interaction.
prompts.ask: Ask before adding a dramatic door cycle for the shot; it must never compromise the functioning airlock merely to improve the reveal.

prompts.title: Verify rules, saves and LAN integration
prompts.read: Existing tests; tools/run_tests.ps1; new task, survival, cassette and room event contracts.
prompts.goal: Add meaningful regression checks and fix cross-system defects without expanding feature scope.
build: Cover the twelve-task role matrix, including solo switching with no bypass; host validation of puzzle moves; duplicate/stale completion; operator release; both task orders; old-save migration and late join.

Measure four-second exposure at several frame rates and sol lengths, with panels open, depleted suit and an airlock fault. Verify global pause rules separately from local menus. Check wear continues and never double-ticks.
Verify six pickup IDs, no remote playback path, a usable damaged Command Room player and offline NASA assets. Test narrative milestones versus recurring maintenance and seen beauty-shot persistence.

Use the discovered Godot binary and project-local test runner. Run focused new suites and affected existing life-support, saves, session, UI and network suites; retain logs. Report actual outcomes and unresolved limitations.
checks: No failing affected suite or unhandled script/import error remains.
Two peers can perform general/specialist tasks concurrently without overwriting state.
Do not report headless tests as evidence of visual quality or subjective playability.
prompts.ask: If the environment lacks a Godot binary or second peer, document the exact missing check and provide a runnable reproduction. Do not fabricate a pass.

prompts.title: Playtest the complete route and deliver the handoff
prompts.deps: Q01; all visual and camera prompts
prompts.read: The final acceptance matrix; changed files; current build/export instructions and source manifest.
prompts.goal: Finish a reviewable solo and co-op release candidate with evidence for all four requested ROI areas.
build: Play a new solo game from Med Bay, collect all six tapes, return to the Command Room player, and finish all twelve tasks by switching specialists. Record each room at damaged, partial and restored states.

Run a host/client session demonstrating wrong-role rejection, a general helper, concurrent room work, late join, disconnect/rejoin, ongoing degradation and airlock danger. Check camera safety while another peer remains active.

Inspect UI at both target resolutions, large text, high contrast and reduced motion. View all six beauty paths; specifically verify flowing dome pipes and intact glass. Check NASA captions/credits offline.

Deliver concise controls, known limitations, balance values, changed-file list, real test logs, source credits and rollback/migration notes. Reconcile any divergence from the approved requirement matrix before declaring completion.
checks: Every acceptance item on the final page has evidence or a specific unresolved blocker.
No placeholder asset, debug-only completion shortcut or inaccessible required specialist ships.
The owner can reproduce the full route with the handoff instructions.
prompts.ask: Ask about unresolved product tradeoffs using concrete evidence. Do not silently mark incomplete gameplay as done or add unrelated polish work.
